questions.question: What is the orbital hybridization and geometry of the acetylide anion formed by deprotonating 1-butyne?

options.label: A
options.text: The lone pair resides in an unhybridized 2p orbital perpendicular to the ring.

options.label: B
options.text: The lone pair resides in an sp³ tetrahedral orbital.

options.label: C
options.text: The carbanionic carbon is sp² hybridized with trigonal planar geometry.

options.label: D
options.text: The carbanionic lone pair resides in an sp hybrid orbital directed linearly at 180° from the C-C single bond.

questions.correct_answer: The carbanionic lone pair resides in an sp hybrid orbital directed linearly at 180° from the C-C single bond.
questions.explanation: The terminal alkyne carbon is sp hybridized; deprotonation retains the sp orbital holding the lone pair close to the nucleus.

questions.question: What is the mechanistic classification of the reaction between sodium acetylide and 1-bromobutane?

options.label: A
options.text: An electrophilic addition across the alkyne triple bond.

options.label: B
options.text: A classic bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) where the sp-carbanion attacks the primary carbon with backside displacement of bromide.

options.label: C
options.text: An E2 elimination yielding butene and acetylene.

options.label: D
options.text: A radical chain substitution initiated by sodium metal.

questions.correct_answer: A classic bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) where the sp-carbanion attacks the primary carbon with backside displacement of bromide.
questions.explanation: Acetylide anions are powerful, linear carbon nucleophiles that displace primary alkyl halides efficiently via SN2.

questions.question: What is the role of the Hg²⁺ catalyst in the acid-catalyzed hydration of alkynes?

options.label: A
options.text: Hg²⁺ acts as a Brønsted base that deprotonates water.

options.label: B
options.text: Hg²⁺ oxidizes the alkyne to a dialdehyde.

options.label: C
options.text: Hg²⁺ reduces the alkyne to an alkane directly.

options.label: D
options.text: Hg²⁺ coordinates to the alkyne π system to form a cyclic mercurinium ion, activating the triple bond toward nucleophilic attack by water.

questions.correct_answer: Hg²⁺ coordinates to the alkyne π system to form a cyclic mercurinium ion, activating the triple bond toward nucleophilic attack by water.
questions.explanation: Mercuric ion electrophilically coordinates to the alkyne π system, greatly accelerating nucleophilic capture by water.

questions.question: What mechanistic sequence converts the transient enol intermediate into the final ketone during alkyne hydration?

options.label: A
options.text: Protonation of the enol π bond at the terminal carbon to form a resonance-stabilized oxocarbenium ion, followed by deprotonation at oxygen.

options.label: B
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of hydroxide on the enol oxygen.

options.label: C
options.text: Direct uncatalyzed intramolecular 1,3-proton transfer through space.

options.label: D
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the O-H bond followed by 1,2-hydrogen shift.

questions.correct_answer: Protonation of the enol π bond at the terminal carbon to form a resonance-stabilized oxocarbenium ion, followed by deprotonation at oxygen.
questions.explanation: Acid-catalyzed tautomerization proceeds through oxocarbenium resonance intermediates to achieve the thermodynamically stable keto form.

questions.question: Why are hindered dialkylboranes such as disiamylborane or 9-BBN used instead of BH₃ for terminal alkyne hydroboration?

options.label: A
options.text: Hindered boranes act as radical initiators.

options.label: B
options.text: Hindered boranes oxidize the alkyne directly to carboxylic acids.

options.label: C
options.text: Steric bulk prevents a second hydroboration across the remaining double bond, cleanly stopping at the mono-alkenylborane intermediate.

options.label: D
options.text: BH₃ is incapable of reacting with alkynes.

questions.correct_answer: Steric bulk prevents a second hydroboration across the remaining double bond, cleanly stopping at the mono-alkenylborane intermediate.
questions.explanation: Bulky dialkylboranes ensure mono-addition to terminal alkynes, allowing subsequent oxidation to yield the aldehyde without over-hydroboration.

questions.question: What is the sequence of elementary steps in the reduction of an internal alkyne with Na in liquid NH₃?

options.label: A
options.text: Concerted syn addition of two sodium atoms followed by water quench.

options.label: B
options.text: Single electron transfer (SET) → radical anion → trans-inversion → protonation by NH₃ → second SET to carbanion → final protonation to trans-alkene.

options.label: C
options.text: Electrophilic addition of amide ion followed by hydride displacement.

options.label: D
options.text: Catalytic hydrogenation on colloidal sodium nanoparticles.

questions.correct_answer: Single electron transfer (SET) → radical anion → trans-inversion → protonation by NH₃ → second SET to carbanion → final protonation to trans-alkene.
questions.explanation: Stepwise single-electron transfers allow the radical anion intermediate to equilibrate to the thermodynamically favored trans configuration.

questions.question: What is the mechanistic function of lead acetate and quinoline 'poisons' in the Lindlar palladium catalyst?

options.label: A
options.text: They selectively deactivate high-energy catalytic sites on palladium, allowing syn-hydrogenation of alkynes to cis-alkenes while preventing further reduction of the alkene.

options.label: B
options.text: They act as phase-transfer catalysts that dissolve palladium.

options.label: C
options.text: They change the reaction mechanism from syn addition to anti addition.

options.label: D
options.text: They oxidize the alkyne to a diketone.

questions.correct_answer: They selectively deactivate high-energy catalytic sites on palladium, allowing syn-hydrogenation of alkynes to cis-alkenes while preventing further reduction of the alkene.
questions.explanation: Catalyst poisoning attenuates catalytic activity so that the reaction stops cleanly at the cis-alkene stage without overreduction to the alkane.

questions.question: In the addition of 2 equivalents of HBr to propyne, why do both bromines attach to the same carbon (geminal dibromide)?

options.label: A
options.text: The secondary bromo-carbocation intermediate [CH₃-C⁺(Br)-CH₃] is strongly resonance-stabilized by lone pair donation from the adjacent bromine atom.

options.label: B
options.text: The reaction proceeds via a cyclic dibromonium dication.

options.label: C
options.text: Steric hindrance prevents bromine from attacking the terminal carbon.

options.label: D
options.text: The terminal carbon is antiaromatic.

questions.correct_answer: The secondary bromo-carbocation intermediate [CH₃-C⁺(Br)-CH₃] is strongly resonance-stabilized by lone pair donation from the adjacent bromine atom.
questions.explanation: Halogen lone pair resonance donation stabilizes the α-halocarbocation intermediate, directing the second addition to the same carbon.

questions.question: Why does ozonolysis of an internal alkyne produce two carboxylic acids rather than aldehydes?

options.label: A
options.text: Carboxylic acids are formed by secondary reaction with zinc.

options.label: B
options.text: Alkynes cannot undergo ozonolysis.

options.label: C
options.text: The high oxidation state of the alkyne carbon (sp) and ozonide intermediate leads to complete oxidative cleavage of all three C-C bonds to carboxylic acids.

options.label: D
options.text: Aldehydes are reduced to acids by ozone.

questions.correct_answer: The high oxidation state of the alkyne carbon (sp) and ozonide intermediate leads to complete oxidative cleavage of all three C-C bonds to carboxylic acids.
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis cleaves all three bonds of the alkyne triple bond, generating carboxylic acid functional groups at each sp carbon.

questions.topic: Alkyne Acidity vs Alkene and Alkane
questions.question: What is the physical basis for the significant acidity of terminal alkynes (pKa ~ 25) compared to alkenes (pKa ~ 44)?

options.label: A
options.text: Alkynes have lower molecular weights than alkenes.

options.label: B
options.text: The acetylide anion is aromatic.

options.label: C
options.text: Terminal alkynes undergo rapid resonance into the triple bond.

options.label: D
options.text: The conjugate base acetylide carbanion holds its lone pair in an sp orbital with 50% s-character, placing negative charge closer to the carbon nucleus.

questions.correct_answer: The conjugate base acetylide carbanion holds its lone pair in an sp orbital with 50% s-character, placing negative charge closer to the carbon nucleus.
questions.explanation: High s-character (50% in sp vs 33% in sp² and 25% in sp³) increases effective nuclear charge felt by lone pair electrons, stabilizing the carbanion.

options.text: A radical chain substitution initiated by sodium metal.

options.label: B
options.text: A classic bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) where the sp-carbanion attacks the primary carbon with backside displacement of bromide.

options.label: C
options.text: An E2 elimination yielding butene and acetylene.

options.label: D
options.text: An electrophilic addition across the alkyne triple bond.

questions.correct_answer: A classic bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) where the sp-carbanion attacks the primary carbon with backside displacement of bromide.
questions.explanation: Acetylide anions are powerful, linear carbon nucleophiles that displace primary alkyl halides efficiently via SN2.

questions.question: What is the role of the Hg²⁺ catalyst in the acid-catalyzed hydration of alkynes?

options.label: A
options.text: Hg²⁺ coordinates to the alkyne π system to form a cyclic mercurinium ion, activating the triple bond toward nucleophilic attack by water.

options.label: B
options.text: Hg²⁺ oxidizes the alkyne to a dialdehyde.

options.label: C
options.text: Hg²⁺ reduces the alkyne to an alkane directly.

options.label: D
options.text: Hg²⁺ acts as a Brønsted base that deprotonates water.

questions.correct_answer: Hg²⁺ coordinates to the alkyne π system to form a cyclic mercurinium ion, activating the triple bond toward nucleophilic attack by water.
questions.explanation: Mercuric ion electrophilically coordinates to the alkyne π system, greatly accelerating nucleophilic capture by water.

questions.question: What mechanistic sequence converts the transient enol intermediate into the final ketone during alkyne hydration?

options.label: A
options.text: Direct uncatalyzed intramolecular 1,3-proton transfer through space.

options.label: B
options.text: Protonation of the enol π bond at the terminal carbon to form a resonance-stabilized oxocarbenium ion, followed by deprotonation at oxygen.

options.label: C
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the O-H bond followed by 1,2-hydrogen shift.

options.label: D
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of hydroxide on the enol oxygen.

questions.correct_answer: Protonation of the enol π bond at the terminal carbon to form a resonance-stabilized oxocarbenium ion, followed by deprotonation at oxygen.
questions.explanation: Acid-catalyzed tautomerization proceeds through oxocarbenium resonance intermediates to achieve the thermodynamically stable keto form.

questions.question: Why are hindered dialkylboranes such as disiamylborane or 9-BBN used instead of BH₃ for terminal alkyne hydroboration?

options.label: A
options.text: Hindered boranes act as radical initiators.

options.label: B
options.text: Steric bulk prevents a second hydroboration across the remaining double bond, cleanly stopping at the mono-alkenylborane intermediate.

options.label: C
options.text: Hindered boranes oxidize the alkyne directly to carboxylic acids.

options.label: D
options.text: BH₃ is incapable of reacting with alkynes.

questions.correct_answer: Steric bulk prevents a second hydroboration across the remaining double bond, cleanly stopping at the mono-alkenylborane intermediate.
questions.explanation: Bulky dialkylboranes ensure mono-addition to terminal alkynes, allowing subsequent oxidation to yield the aldehyde without over-hydroboration.

questions.question: What is the sequence of elementary steps in the reduction of an internal alkyne with Na in liquid NH₃?

options.label: A
options.text: Concerted syn addition of two sodium atoms followed by water quench.

options.label: B
options.text: Electrophilic addition of amide ion followed by hydride displacement.

options.label: C
options.text: Catalytic hydrogenation on colloidal sodium nanoparticles.

options.label: D
options.text: Single electron transfer (SET) → radical anion → trans-inversion → protonation by NH₃ → second SET to carbanion → final protonation to trans-alkene.

questions.correct_answer: Single electron transfer (SET) → radical anion → trans-inversion → protonation by NH₃ → second SET to carbanion → final protonation to trans-alkene.
questions.explanation: Stepwise single-electron transfers allow the radical anion intermediate to equilibrate to the thermodynamically favored trans configuration.

questions.question: Why does ozonolysis of an internal alkyne produce two carboxylic acids rather than aldehydes?

options.label: A
options.text: Aldehydes are reduced to acids by ozone.

options.label: B
options.text: Alkynes cannot undergo ozonolysis.

options.label: C
options.text: Carboxylic acids are formed by secondary reaction with zinc.

options.label: D
options.text: The high oxidation state of the alkyne carbon (sp) and ozonide intermediate leads to complete oxidative cleavage of all three C-C bonds to carboxylic acids.

questions.correct_answer: The high oxidation state of the alkyne carbon (sp) and ozonide intermediate leads to complete oxidative cleavage of all three C-C bonds to carboxylic acids.
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis cleaves all three bonds of the alkyne triple bond, generating carboxylic acid functional groups at each sp carbon.

questions.topic: Alkyne Acidity vs Alkene and Alkane
questions.question: What is the physical basis for the significant acidity of terminal alkynes (pKa ~ 25) compared to alkenes (pKa ~ 44)?

options.label: A
options.text: Terminal alkynes undergo rapid resonance into the triple bond.

options.label: B
options.text: Alkynes have lower molecular weights than alkenes.

options.label: C
options.text: The conjugate base acetylide carbanion holds its lone pair in an sp orbital with 50% s-character, placing negative charge closer to the carbon nucleus.

options.label: D
options.text: The acetylide anion is aromatic.

questions.correct_answer: The conjugate base acetylide carbanion holds its lone pair in an sp orbital with 50% s-character, placing negative charge closer to the carbon nucleus.
questions.explanation: High s-character (50% in sp vs 33% in sp² and 25% in sp³) increases effective nuclear charge felt by lone pair electrons, stabilizing the carbanion.

questions.question: What is the orbital hybridization and geometry of the acetylide anion formed by deprotonating 1-butyne?

options.label: A
options.text: The carbanionic carbon is sp² hybridized with trigonal planar geometry.

options.label: B
options.text: The lone pair resides in an unhybridized 2p orbital perpendicular to the ring.

options.label: C
options.text: The carbanionic lone pair resides in an sp hybrid orbital directed linearly at 180° from the C-C single bond.

options.label: D
options.text: The lone pair resides in an sp³ tetrahedral orbital.

questions.correct_answer: The carbanionic lone pair resides in an sp hybrid orbital directed linearly at 180° from the C-C single bond.
questions.explanation: The terminal alkyne carbon is sp hybridized; deprotonation retains the sp orbital holding the lone pair close to the nucleus.

questions.question: What is the mechanistic function of lead acetate and quinoline 'poisons' in the Lindlar palladium catalyst?

options.label: A
options.text: They selectively deactivate high-energy catalytic sites on palladium, allowing syn-hydrogenation of alkynes to cis-alkenes while preventing further reduction of the alkene.

options.label: B
options.text: They change the reaction mechanism from syn addition to anti addition.

options.label: C
options.text: They act as phase-transfer catalysts that dissolve palladium.

options.label: D
options.text: They oxidize the alkyne to a diketone.

questions.correct_answer: They selectively deactivate high-energy catalytic sites on palladium, allowing syn-hydrogenation of alkynes to cis-alkenes while preventing further reduction of the alkene.
questions.explanation: Catalyst poisoning attenuates catalytic activity so that the reaction stops cleanly at the cis-alkene stage without overreduction to the alkane.

questions.question: In the addition of 2 equivalents of HBr to propyne, why do both bromines attach to the same carbon (geminal dibromide)?

options.label: A
options.text: The reaction proceeds via a cyclic dibromonium dication.

options.label: B
options.text: The secondary bromo-carbocation intermediate [CH₃-C⁺(Br)-CH₃] is strongly resonance-stabilized by lone pair donation from the adjacent bromine atom.

options.label: C
options.text: Steric hindrance prevents bromine from attacking the terminal carbon.

options.label: D
options.text: The terminal carbon is antiaromatic.

questions.correct_answer: The secondary bromo-carbocation intermediate [CH₃-C⁺(Br)-CH₃] is strongly resonance-stabilized by lone pair donation from the adjacent bromine atom.
questions.explanation: Halogen lone pair resonance donation stabilizes the α-halocarbocation intermediate, directing the second addition to the same carbon.
